handoff: review#2 approve: F1 rework holds (picker step_type/effective_mode match the command, regression test). AC1–AC6 met at S1; AC7 left for QA. Suite 1252 pass, typecheck green. Minor only: pickers still offer edge cases the command refuses (claim held elsewhere, no worktree; mode picker offers not_started/corrupt), test gaps (manual-ready offered; AC2 tick launch), B55 wording for an explicit slice key, cmd.open/workflow hints for slice 14 (same release, D1).

findings.title: Picker can still offer units the command refuses (claim held elsewhere, no worktree)
findings.detail:
`startable.applies` does not exclude a unit whose claim another heartbeat holds (`u.claim.state === "other"`), and the command refuses that unit at :42 through refuseIfHeldElsewhere. It also does not exclude a unit with no worktree on this checkout, which the command refuses at :51 (no_worktree). Both are edge cases. The common F1 case is fixed.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Also require u.claim.state !== 'other' (and a local worktree when the view has one) in applies.

findings.title: Mode picker offers not_started and corrupt stories that editMode refuses
findings.detail:
`editable('mode').applies` accepts any story unit with status !== 'done'. editMode goes through runHumanVerb/started(), which refuses not_started and corrupt units. The listing in `command` also always suggests --auto, even for a story that is already in auto mode.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Exclude not_started and corrupt from applies, and suggest the opposite of the story's effective_mode.

findings.title: No test that a manual ready agent-step unit is offered and an auto one is not
findings.detail:
The picker tests cover an attended-parked unit (offered) and a manual unit at a check step (left out). The manual && step_type==='agent' branch of applies (story-start.ts:23) has no test that offers it, and no test leaves out an auto unit ready at an agent step.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add both cases to story-start.test.ts.

findings.title: AC2 'next tick runs gh-N in auto' only asserts state.mode
findings.detail:
Carried over from review#1 F3. The test checks state.mode after the tick, not that the tick launches the unit in auto (in that fixture the agent is already running, MO3).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Use a story parked or ready in manual mode, switch it to --auto, tick, and assert the runner launch.

findings.title: Explicit slice key with --auto/--manual now edits the story (old mode refused story_only)
findings.detail:
B55 speaks only of a person in a slice worktree. The new behaviour is consistent with MO1 and B55's intent, and human.test.ts:465 pins it, but the spec does not state it.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Make B55's wording say that a slice key means its story too (slice 15's PRD and spec wording).

findings.title: Printed hints still name removed commands (slice 14)
findings.detail:
cmd.open is used in inbox items.ts:198, agent-unit.ts:35,47 and cockpit.ts:95 (prefix match). cmd.workflow is used in update.ts:47 and decide/steps.ts:32. assets/config.yaml:48-49 and the norn SKILL.md:12 also name these commands. Each hint now prints a command that does not exist. Out of scope here; slice 14 must land in the same release (D1).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Track in slice 14.

findings.title: No-op JSON omits `previous`; small naming nits
findings.detail:
The no-op returns {unit, mode, changed:false} and has no `previous` field, unlike the changed case. In `editable(verb)`, the parameter `verb` shadows the rule's own `verb` field. The comment at :94, 'as before: …', points at deleted code.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Add previous to the no-op shape; rename the parameter to kind; reword the comment.
